high.title: Real Estate Association Chairman: State Bank of Vietnam says lending rates have decreased, but in reality businesses still have to borrow at higher rates
high.summary: Le Hoang Chau, Chairman of Ho Chi Minh City Real Estate Association (HoREA), highlighted a key discrepancy between official SBV policy and market reality. While the State Bank of Vietnam issued Circular 08 amending Circular 22 - allowing 20% of State Treasury deposits to count toward bank liquidity (excluding only 80% instead of 100%) - businesses still face high borrowing costs. The SBV announced 15% credit growth target for 2026, significantly lower than 19.1% in 2025. Real estate credit grew over 24% last year according to official SBV data. This policy adjustment should theoretically improve commercial bank liquidity and support lending capacity, but the transmission mechanism to actual lending rates remains problematic. For FX and bond traders, this signals continued monetary policy challenges in Vietnam, with potential implications for VND stability and government bond demand as banks may still prefer safer assets over lending.

high.title: The "Silent Disease" of the Banking System Pushing Interest Rates Higher: Will the State Bank of Vietnam's "Pressure Valve" Be Strong Enough to Cool Down?
high.summary: Expert analysis reveals structural issues in Vietnam's banking system that are keeping interest rates elevated despite SBV policy efforts. The system faces increasing dependence on State Treasury deposits for liquidity, alongside significant maturity mismatches between short-term deposit mobilization and medium to long-term credit demand. Both interbank market rates and retail deposit/lending rates have shown strong volatility since early 2026, while deposit mobilization growth has slowed at many banks. The SBV's recent technical adjustment to the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) calculation represents an attempt to address liquidity pressures, but questions remain about the effectiveness of this "pressure valve." The analysis suggests these structural problems may be core reasons why interest rate levels remain anchored high, with implications for monetary policy transmission, VND exchange rate stability, and government bond yields.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Intervenes in Deposit Rate Increases
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam has issued urgent directives to regional branches to strictly monitor and control deposit rate increases by commercial banks. The SBV requires branches to directly inspect compliance with rate reduction directives aimed at supporting businesses and economic growth. Banks found violating or not properly implementing these policies face immediate action and reporting to banking supervision authorities. This intervention comes as MB Securities research shows actual over-the-counter deposit rates remain significantly higher than published rates, with some banks offering rates through special agreements that exceed official levels. The SBV's "hot" directive on rate reduction represents an escalation in monetary policy enforcement. For traders, this signals potential volatility in the interbank market and government bond yields as banks may be forced to adjust their funding costs, potentially impacting VND liquidity and exchange rate stability.

medium.title: "I deposited savings at 8%/year interest rate but still decided to withdraw it all and re-deposit"
medium.summary: Customers are actively seeking higher deposit rates as banks compete for funding. Some banks now offer 8.5-9% rates for deposits and CDs, with additional bonuses through staff referral codes adding 1-1.5% more. This rate competition reflects tight liquidity conditions and banks' funding pressures.

medium.title: Tax Deputy Director: We have information on 250 million bank accounts, unusual transactions or tax evasion can be reviewed immediately
medium.summary: Tax authorities now have access to 250 million bank accounts (200 million personal accounts) through digital invoice systems and bank connectivity. This enhanced financial surveillance capability could impact capital flows and banking system transparency.

medium.title: Gold ring and gold bar prices afternoon 21/5: All decrease compared to morning
medium.summary: Gold prices in Vietnam retreated in afternoon trading after morning gains, with SJC gold bars trading at 159.4-162.4 million VND/tael. International gold pressured by stronger USD and high oil prices affecting Fed rate cut expectations.

medium.title: Chairman declares return to the 'race track', VNDirect shares hit ceiling

medium.title: Foreign investors suddenly net sell nearly 6,400 billion VND in mid-May week
medium.summary: Foreign investors net sold 6,377 billion VND across all exchanges during the week, with HoSE bearing the brunt at 6,281 billion VND net selling. Heavy selling pressure focused on banks and bluechips including ACB, MSB, VIC, HPG.

medium.title: A steel industry stock hits ceiling to 2-year high
medium.summary: TVN shares of Vietnam Steel Corporation hit ceiling price at 10,600 VND (+13.98%), reaching highest level in 2 years with record volume of 4.7 million shares traded, despite legal issues surrounding related entities.
